note: Alternating tripod, the insect walk: the front and hind legs of one side step with the middle leg of the other, so three feet always hold a triangle under the body. Each tripod ripples a little from front to back so six footfalls do not land as two. A weevil is heavy and short-legged, so the stride is small against its leg span and the body rolls side to side over each tripod; the head nods with the step and pitches a touch positive (nose-down) to stay level as the body dips.
